questions.nlq: I request a comprehensive report identifying the top-ranked products within each category based on complaint frequency, displaying their associated dates and prices for items where the category average price exceeds twenty dollars.

meanings.hidden_knowledge: When referencing dates for products, I mean the dates when each product first became available on the market, not when they were discontinued. This helps track how long products have been in circulation rather than when they left it.
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH CategoryAverage AS (
    SELECT product_category_code
    FROM Products
    GROUP BY product_category_code
    HAVING AVG(product_price) > 20
),
ProductComplaintRank AS (
    SELECT 
        p.product_category_code,
        p.date_product_first_available,
        p.product_price,
        COUNT(c.complaint_id) as complaint_count,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY p.product_category_code 
            ORDER BY COUNT(c.complaint_id) DESC
        ) as complaint_rank
    FROM Products p
    INNER JOIN Complaints c ON p.product_id = c.product_id
    WHERE p.product_category_code IN (SELECT product_category_code FROM CategoryAverage)
    GROUP BY p.product_category_code, p.date_product_first_available, p.product_price, p.product_id
)
SELECT 
    date_product_first_available,
    product_price
FROM ProductComplaintRank
WHERE complaint_rank = 1;

    SELECT 
        product_category_code,
        AVG(product_price) AS avg_price

    HAVING AVG(product_price) > 20
),
ProductComplaintCounts AS (
    SELECT 
        p.product_id,
        p.product_category_code,
        p.date_product_discontinued,
        p.product_price,
        COUNT(c.complaint_id) AS complaint_count
    FROM Products p
    LEFT JOIN Complaints c ON p.product_id = c.product_id
    WHERE p.product_category_code IN (SELECT product_category_code FROM CategoryAveragePrice)
    GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_category_code, p.date_product_discontinued, p.product_price
),
RankedProducts AS (
    SELECT 
        product_id,
        product_category_code,
        date_product_discontinued,
        product_price,
        complaint_count,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_category_code ORDER BY complaint_count DESC) AS rank
    FROM ProductComplaintCounts
)
SELECT 
    date_product_discontinued,
    product_price
FROM RankedProducts
WHERE rank = 1

FROM complaints_qtr c

questions.nlq: Hey! Could you help me out? I need to know which staff members have handled the most complaints along with the customer phone numbers from their cases—show me the count and just the phone numbers, but only for staff who've closed at least 3 complaints!

meanings.hidden_knowledge: When I say customer phone numbers, I mean the phone numbers of the customers who submitted the complaints, not the phone numbers of the staff members who handled them.
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH ClosedComplaintsPerStaff AS (
    SELECT 
        c.staff_id,
        COUNT(*) AS complaint_count
    FROM Complaints c
    WHERE c.complaint_status_code = 'Closed'
    GROUP BY c.staff_id
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
)
SELECT 
    ccp.complaint_count,
    cu.phone_number
FROM Complaints c
JOIN ClosedComplaintsPerStaff ccp ON c.staff_id = ccp.staff_id
JOIN Customers cu ON c.customer_id = cu.customer_id
WHERE c.complaint_status_code = 'Closed'
ORDER BY ccp.complaint_count DESC, cu.phone_number

meanings.hidden_knowledge: When I say customer phone numbers, I mean the phone numbers of the customers whose complaints were handled—basically the contact info for the people who complained, which is different from the staff contact information.

    cu.phone_number
FROM (

        staff_id,
        COUNT(*) AS complaint_count
    FROM Complaints
    WHERE complaint_status_code = 'Closed'
    GROUP BY staff_id
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
) AS st_closed_counts
JOIN Complaints c ON st_closed_counts.staff_id = c.staff_id
JOIN Customers cu ON c.customer_id = cu.customer_id
WHERE c.complaint_status_code = 'Closed'

FROM Customers c

GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.address_line_1

ORDER BY open_complaint_count DESC;

    JOIN Customers c ON comp.customer_id = c.customer_id
    WHERE comp.complaint_status_code = 'Closed'
      AND comp.date_complaint_closed IS NOT NULL

    FROM state_avg_resolution
    ORDER BY avg_resolution_days DESC
